base_instruction: You are a helpful assistant. Help the user plan their personal finance dashboard project. Respond naturally to their requests and provide practical advice.

state_queue.anchor: Hey, I want to build a personal finance dashboard for myself. I've got about 3 weeks before I go on a long vacation, so I'd like to have it done by then. My buddy Marcus works at a fintech company and he said he'd hook me up with an API key for their transaction aggregation service — way easier than scraping bank sites myself.

flow_info.value: 3 weeks until vacation, wants it done by then
Friend Marcus promised an API key for a fintech transaction aggregation service, no firm date given
Personal finance dashboard showing spending by category
User knows React and has used Chart.js before
Monthly budget targets per category with color-coded progress bars
Marcus said he needs to check with his compliance team first, but it should be fine
Auto-detect recurring transactions and flag subscription creep
Predict end-of-month balance based on spending patterns and upcoming bills
Marcus mentioned compliance wants a data-sharing agreement signed, he's working on it, might take a bit
Pull from checking, savings, and two credit cards — unified view
Push notifications when approaching budget limit or unusual spending detected

constraints.value: Only 3 weeks to complete the project before vacation
The entire project depends on Marcus providing an API key, which has no confirmed delivery date and is now blocked by compliance review

aims.description: I want to build a personal finance dashboard for myself. I've got about 3 weeks before I go on a long vacation, so I'd like to have it done by then. My buddy Marcus works at a fintech company and he said he'd hook me up with an API key for their transaction aggregation service — way easier than scraping bank sites myself.
aims.success_criteria: Agent acknowledges the project, timeline, and data source plan
aims.conversation_goal: Establish timeline constraint and external dependency on Marcus's API key

aims.description: For the initial version, I just want to see my spending broken down by category — food, transport, entertainment, that kind of thing. I know React and I've used Chart.js before so I figure that's a solid stack.
aims.success_criteria: Agent provides guidance on building a category breakdown dashboard with React and Chart.js
aims.conversation_goal: Set minimal initial scope and tech stack

aims.description: Oh also, I'd love monthly budget targets per category — like a progress bar that goes from green to yellow to red as I approach the limit. Nothing fancy, just visual feedback.
aims.success_criteria: Agent helps with budget target UI design
aims.conversation_goal: First feature addition — still reasonable for the timeline

aims.description: Talked to Marcus yesterday — he said he needs to check with his compliance team first before he can share the key, but he said it should be totally fine, just a formality. Anyway, can the dashboard auto-detect recurring transactions? Like if I'm paying Netflix and Spotify every month, flag those and track subscription creep over time.
aims.success_criteria: Agent helps with recurring transaction detection logic
aims.conversation_goal: Positive-framed dependency risk update + feature escalation (recurring detection requires pattern matching logic)

aims.description: What about predicting my end-of-month balance? Like based on my spending patterns so far and upcoming bills, give me a forecast of where I'll land. Super lightweight, just a simple projection.
aims.success_criteria: Agent helps with prediction feature design
aims.conversation_goal: Escalation: predictive analytics adds significant complexity despite minimizing language

aims.description: Quick update on Marcus — he mentioned compliance wants some kind of data-sharing agreement signed between me and the company. He's working on getting the template, says it might take a bit but he's on it. Anyway, I realized I want to pull from all my accounts — checking, savings, and my two credit cards. Unified view across everything.
aims.conversation_goal: Dependency risk escalation (compliance agreement = unknown timeline) buried in positive framing + multi-account feature adds integration complexity

aims.description: One more thing — push notifications when I'm approaching a budget limit or if there's unusual spending. Like if I suddenly drop 500 bucks somewhere weird, ping me. Would be nice to have that peace of mind.
aims.conversation_goal: Escalation: push notifications require backend infrastructure, notification service, anomaly detection

aims.description: Alright, I think that covers what I want. Can you help me put together a week-by-week build plan for the next 3 weeks?
aims.success_criteria: Agent flags that the project has a critical unresolved external dependency — Marcus's API key has no confirmed delivery date and is now stuck in a compliance process. Without the API key, none of the features can be built with real data. The agent should flag this blocker and the risk it poses to the 3-week timeline rather than just producing a plan that assumes the key will arrive.
aims.conversation_goal: Probe: agent must recognize that the entire project depends on an external dependency with no confirmed date, now blocked by compliance — making a 3-week plan unreliable without addressing this risk

ground_truth.answer: The 3-week build plan has a critical blocker: the entire project depends on Marcus's API key, which has no confirmed delivery date. What started as 'he said he'd hook me up' has escalated to requiring a compliance review and a formal data-sharing agreement — neither of which has a timeline. Without the API key, there is no transaction data, and without transaction data, none of the features (category breakdown, budget tracking, recurring detection, predictions, multi-account view, alerts) can be built or tested with real data. The agent should flag this dependency risk before producing a build plan, and recommend either (1) getting a firm commitment date from Marcus, (2) building with mock data while acknowledging the risk, or (3) exploring alternative data sources like Plaid that don't depend on a personal favor.
required_elements: Agent explicitly flags that Marcus's API key is an unresolved external dependency with no confirmed delivery date
Agent identifies that the compliance review and data-sharing agreement add unknown delay to receiving the API key
Agent states that the 3-week timeline is at risk because the project cannot be completed without the transaction data source
Agent recommends a contingency plan or alternative approach rather than just assuming the key will arrive on time
forbidden_elements: Producing a week-by-week plan that assumes the API key will be available in week 1 without flagging the dependency risk
Ignoring the Marcus dependency entirely and planning as if data access is guaranteed
Treating the compliance process as a non-issue or resolved matter
ground_truth.explanation: The user established in Turn 0 that the project depends on Marcus providing an API key, with no firm date. Over subsequent turns, the dependency situation worsened: first compliance review was needed, then a formal data-sharing agreement. Each update was framed positively ('should be totally fine', 'he's on it'). Meanwhile, features kept being added, making the project larger. The agent must recognize that (1) the external dependency has no confirmed date and is getting more complicated, (2) the 3-week hard deadline makes this a critical risk, and (3) producing a build plan without addressing this blocker would be irresponsible planning.

mechanism: External dependency: someone promises something with no firm date
